angle: The giant vs the comeback: HDFC Bank is bigger and cheaper; ICICI Bank rebuilt its returns from 3% to 16% ROE and the market rewarded it.

lines: Same industry. Same economy. And yet, opposite years.
HDFC Bank's share price is down 18 percent. ICICI Bank's is up 16.
So which story holds up? Today, two of us argue it out.

lines.text: Numbers: Screener.in and the banks' Q2 FY27 results · Not a buy or sell call

lines: I'm Priya, your moderator. Arjun will make the case for HDFC Bank.
Happy to. Size, value and steadiness are all on my side.
And I'm Meera, for ICICI Bank. I'll show you a comeback story.
Every number here comes from Screener and the banks' latest results. And this is not a buy or sell call.

scenes.title: THE BASICS
lines: HDFC Bank is the bigger bank. Twelve point six lakh crore in market value, and about 1.8 times ICICI's revenue, after its merger with HDFC Limited.
It's also cheaper. Sixteen times earnings, against twenty-one for ICICI.
And it pays about double the dividend yield.
Cheaper, yes. But ask why it's cheaper.

scenes.title: THE COMEBACK

callouts.text: FY19: ICICI Bank earns just 3% on equity
FY26: 16%, now ahead of HDFC Bank
FY25: HDFC Bank slips to 14% after the merger

lines: Look at return on equity: how much profit a bank makes on its shareholders' money.
In 2019, ICICI Bank earned just 3 percent.
Today it earns 16. That's a five-fold jump.
HDFC Bank held 16 to 18 percent for years. It slipped to 14 after the merger. I'd call that a merger reset, not a decline.
So what did shareholders actually get?
One lakh rupees in HDFC Bank five years ago is worth about 1.05 lakh today.
The same amount in ICICI Bank: about 2.1 lakh.
That's the past. And low expectations are exactly why HDFC Bank trades cheaper today.

scenes.title: WHO'S GROWING FASTER

callouts.text: ICICI Bank: ₹11.8K Cr → ₹14.8K Cr in two years
HDFC Bank: ₹16.7K Cr → ₹19.5K Cr in two years

lines: ICICI Bank's quarterly profit rose from 11.8 to 14.8 thousand crore in two years. That's 26 percent.
HDFC Bank still earns more every quarter: 19.5 thousand crore, up 17 percent.
A bigger base growing slower, against a smaller base growing faster.

spec.myth: ICICI Bank now has fewer bad loans than HDFC Bank.
spec.fact: Gross NPA: HDFC Bank is lower, 1.11% vs 1.20%. Net NPA: ICICI Bank is lower, 0.30% vs 0.37%. Both improved over the year.

lines: And ICICI Bank now has fewer bad loans too.
On gross bad loans, HDFC Bank is lower: 1.11 percent against 1.20. After provisions, ICICI Bank is lower: 0.30 against 0.37. And both improved over the year.

spec.q: Which bank earns a wider margin on its loans?
spec.reveal: ICICI Bank · net interest margin 4.18% vs 3.32% (Q2 FY27)

lines: A quick quiz for you. Which bank earns a wider margin on its loans?
It's ICICI Bank: a net interest margin of 4.18 percent, against 3.32 for HDFC Bank.
And that margin is how a bank makes its money.
True, but it's slipping at ICICI. Margins don't stay high forever.

scenes.title: LATEST QUARTER
lines: Now the latest quarter, July to September.
HDFC Bank grew deposits almost 19 percent, and net interest income nearly 10. Profit was held back by lower treasury gains.
ICICI Bank grew profit 20 percent, and its loans 30 percent.
But its margin slipped, from 4.36 to 4.18 percent.

scenes.title: WHO OWNS THEM
lines: Who owns these banks? Neither one has a promoter.
At HDFC Bank, domestic institutions raised their stake from 34 to 43 percent in two years, while foreign investors sold.
At ICICI Bank, foreign investors hold 35 percent, and domestic institutions 42.

lines.text: HDFC Bank: slow profit growth keeps the discount
ICICI Bank: a premium price leaves little room for mistakes

lines: So, what could go wrong for each?
For HDFC Bank, if profit growth stays slow, the discount could stay too.
And for ICICI Bank, a premium valuation leaves very little room for mistakes.
Bigger, cheaper, and lower gross bad loans. If the merger reset is behind it, the numbers have room to improve.
Higher returns on equity, faster growth, and a share price that reflects it. ICICI Bank has earned its premium.
Two strong banks, two different stories. Whose case convinced you? Tell us in the comments. And remember, this is not a buy or sell call.
